newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials rush to new high.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials rush to new high.

text.p: Zimbabwe industrial shares surged on Thursday to a remarkable new high, putting the index in sight of another key level -- 11,000 points.
Dealers said that strong year results from Barclays sparked bullish sentiment about other major companies' performance and propelled stocks higher.
Barclays posted earnings per share for the year ended December 31 of 130.5 cents compared to 79.9 cents.

"It suddenly took off," one dealer said. "It was mainly driven by Barclays results which is a good barometer for other companies. Their results generally confirmed what sentiment had been for a while," he added.
The 57-share industrial index closed 455.80 points, or nearly five percent, stronger at 10,659.8.
Barclays finished 600 cents up at 4,000 cents, FMB was 600 cents stronger at 6,500, Delta was 100 cents up at 1,700 and Zimpapers added 100 cents to 3,000 cents.
Dealers said the market was likely to remain very buoyant this week and maybe carry its bull run into next week.
"Maybe the index won't move so sharply every day, but the buoyancy will certainly be there," a dealer said.

The dull bullion price, however, held mining shares in check and they traded mixed with the index finishing weaker. Dealers said no positive moves were expected in the near future unless the gold price surprised by bouncing.
The seven-share mining index lost 12.67 points to 928.46. Bindura added 10 cents to 685 cents, Rio Tinto shed 100 cents to 2,400 cents, Falcon lost 100 cents to 1,100 cents and Ashanti was unchanged.
